Pause work without losing your place

Push the queue when interrupted, or select a few tasks to push. Open the frame to edit or restore tasks. Once empty, the frame can be deleted from its details; Clear history removes only empty frames, not their tasks.

Drag a task onto the timeline or tap to set a time. Use zero duration for a point in time. Tap +N to see all overlapping events. Checking a daily event completes only that occurrence. The schedule editor supports multiple reminders, including a specific time for one occurrence. Check notification permissions in Settings.

Draw arrows from prerequisites towards a goal. Create template nodes or link existing tasks and specific daily occurrences. Add to queue creates tasks only for templates. Linked tasks stay in place; saving a frame keeps a read-only snapshot of each link.

Add classes manually or import your school timetable. Review the term, first Monday, weeks and periods before saving. Imported classes appear on Today. Importing again replaces only that school’s classes in the selected term.

Choose a calendar date to count days until or since it. Countdowns do not reserve time or schedule notifications. Hide a tab in Settings → Layout without losing access to its page under Feature shortcuts.

The planner works without a model. To chat, configure your service and key in Settings. Tapping Send contacts that service. Sharing other pages or notes requires permission; a proposed change does not alter your schedule until you review and apply it.

Start, scroll or use another StackLife page, then return here and stop. Leaving the foreground ends capture. Starting again replaces the previous report. Only timings for the main window are measured, not screen contents or display FPS.
